attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, summarising BIG-bench and endorsing the summary.

semantics.note: Reading 'not at all' as a typo for 'not all' fits the context. The proposition records the BIG-bench finding and the limited link to his earlier essay.

contract.note: Fair, ordinary reading. It tests only whether gains were uneven across tasks in the original report, not every argument in the 'wall' essay. The typo reading is reasonable.

evidence.note: Original June 9, 2022 BIG-bench preprint. It says that on some tasks performance improves reliably with scale while on others it shows no improvement.

reviews.rationale: The original BIG-bench report says directly that some tasks improve with scale and others do not, which meets the support condition. The paper's caveats (metric choice may hide gradual progress, some tasks show sudden breakthroughs) do not undo this. The wider vindication of the essay is outside the contract's scope.

attribution.note: Marcus's own tweet, quoted and endorsed in his own post as his predictions.

semantics.note: A firm 'will be crucial' under the antecedent 'whenever AGI comes'. The antecedent is kept and no deadline is added.

contract.note: Requiring broadly accepted AGI and evidence of central dependence is a reasonable, ordinary reading of 'crucial'. Excluding tokenization is appropriate.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement of GPT-6 Astra. It does not establish broadly accepted AGI and says nothing about a type/token mechanism.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent (a broadly accepted AGI) is not established in the packet, and there is no architectural evidence about a type/token distinction. A conditional forecast with an unknown antecedent and no deadline cannot be scored. The packet lists the company announcement as counterevidence, but it is context only.

attribution.note: Marcus's own tweet, quoted and endorsed in his own post.

semantics.note: A firm 'will be crucial' conditioned on AGI arriving. The antecedent is kept and no deadline is stated.

contract.note: Reading 'symbolic knowledge' as explicitly represented knowledge and 'crucial' as central dependence is fair. The broad-acceptance safeguard for AGI is reasonable.

evidence.note: Scientific American (Sept 2026) reports disagreement over whether AGI has arrived. It does not establish the antecedent and does not test symbolic knowledge.

reviews.rationale: No broadly accepted AGI is shown in the packet, so the antecedent is unknown. There is also no architectural evidence about large-scale symbolic knowledge. The forecast has no deadline and has not been triggered, so it is not scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own tweet, quoted and endorsed in his own post.

semantics.note: A firm 'will be crucial' conditioned on 'whenever AGI comes'. The antecedent is kept.

contract.note: Reading 'explicit cognitive models' as internal representations of entities, relations and states the system uses is ordinary and fair. 'Crucial' is read as central dependence.

evidence.note: IBM explainer (updated July 2026) says there is no academic consensus on what counts as AGI. It is background only.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not show that a broadly accepted AGI has arrived, and has no evidence about explicit cognitive models in such a system. With the antecedent unknown and no deadline, the forecast is not scored.
